difficulty.heading: DIFFICULTY
difficulty.note: Changes the judge and prosecution — not the case. Applies to every trial.

easy.label: Easy
easy.description: The judge explains rulings and gives you room to find your footing. The prosecution argues plainly, without tricks.

medium.label: Medium
medium.description: Standard courtroom conduct. The judge is even-handed, and the prosecution argues competently and pushes back when warranted.

hard.label: Hard
hard.description: The judge holds you strictly to procedure and courtroom decorum. The prosecution is sharp, aggressive, and looks for every opening.

tutorial.s1Body: You're about to argue a real case. A judge presides, an opposing counsel argues against you, and witnesses testify, all reacting to what you actually say and do. Let's walk through the basics first.
tutorial.s2Body: The trial moves through phases — opening statements, witness examinations, closing arguments. Each phase has a timer, and the header always shows whose turn it is. When it's your turn, the input box at the bottom lights up and waits for you.
tutorial.s3Body: If the other side says something improper — leading a witness, asking about something irrelevant, badgering — tap Object and pick a reason. The judge rules immediately: sustained or overruled. You can object even outside your own turn.
tutorial.s4Body: During examination phases, call a witness and ask them questions — they'll answer based on their actual testimony, not scripted lines. You can also submit evidence exhibits to support your questions or arguments.
tutorial.s5Body: See the microphone icon in the input box? Tap it and just speak — your statement or question gets transcribed automatically. Handy for opening statements or when typing feels slow.
tutorial.s6Body: That's everything you need. Pick your case, choose your side, and make your argument — the verdict is based entirely on how the trial actually goes.

customIntro.title: Welcome to My Cases
customIntro.sub: Your own private cases, played like any case on the Case Board.
customIntro.intro: Build a case from a real or made-up file, then step into court. Interview the witnesses, go to trial against an opposing counsel, and find out where the other side is likely to hit you, so you can rehearse before it counts.
customIntro.step1: Create a case. Tap "Create New Custom Case" and choose how to build it (below).
customIntro.step2: Review and edit. Check witnesses, evidence and details, and fix anything. Nothing is saved until you say so.
customIntro.step3: Interview witnesses. Open the saved case, pick your side and question the witnesses. They only know what their details say.
customIntro.step4: Go to trial. Same trial as the Case Board: jury, opening, examination, objections and a verdict.
customIntro.fromFileBody: Upload a case-file PDF (up to 10 MB) or paste your notes, and choose the side you will argue. The game builds the witnesses, evidence and timeline, plus an Opposing playbook: where the other side will attack, the questions they could ask, and how you can answer.
customIntro.works: Works best with clear facts, statements, exhibits and dates.
customIntro.formBody: Write the case, evidence and witnesses yourself, step by step. You get the same trial either way.
customIntro.know1: Your cases are private to you. Use the pencil on a case to edit it later.
customIntro.know2: The file reading can get things wrong. Check what it built against your documents, especially names, dates and quotes.
customIntro.know3: Uploaded PDFs are processed by Google's Gemini and deleted from our storage once the case is built. Redact client names and anything privileged first. There is a daily limit on case building.
customIntro.reopen: You can reopen this any time from "How do custom cases work?"
